title: IF...ELSE Statement 2
code:
#Calculating Weekly Wages of the employees

totalHours = 45
hourlyWage = 20

if totalHours <= 40:
    totalWages = hourlyWage*totalHours
else:
    overtime = totalHours - 40
    totalWages = hourlyWage*40 + (1.5*hourlyWage)*overtime
print(totalWages)

lines.explanation: In this statement, integer '45' is assigned to the variable 'totalHours'. This variable represents the number of hours an employee has worked in a given week.
Here, integer '20' is assigned to the variable 'hourlyWage'. This is to take in the Hourly Wages of an employee as input
This statement checks if the value of 'totalHours' is less than or equal to 40. In other words, it checks if the employee has worked for 40 hours or less?
If employee has worked for 40 hours or less, total wages would be a product of wages-per-hour and number of hours worked in that week
If the employee has worked for more than 40 hours in that week then this 'else' statement will be executed

First it needs to check how many hours above the standard 40 hours has employee worked. This is because the employee will be paid the normal hourly wages upto 40 hours and 1.5 times the hourly wages for hours above 40 hours. The number of hours worked above 40 hours will be stored in the variable 'overtime'
The total wages is calculated by adding the wages for upto 40 hours and the wages for overtime hours
This statement simply prints the total wages of an employee as output
